IR.rationale: A rise in intermediate yields relative to policy rates signals a repricing of the rate path. It erodes the duration-heavy USD EM sovereign index and tightens funding for leveraged high-yield issuers.

B.rationale: Tightening investment-grade spreads together with strong recent HY returns marks easy credit conditions. Illiquid credit returns are positively autocorrelated at weekly horizons, so this state carries forward.

V.rationale: Elevated equity implied volatility proxies for the price of risk. High risk premia predict higher subsequent expected returns on risky credit, as well as near-term stress.

AP.rationale: Equity markets incorporate firm and EM country information faster than bond markets, so stocks lead high-yield and EM bond returns. Joint strength in US and EM equities is a risk-on signal.

ST.rationale: Equity cross-sectional style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to aggregate credit index returns.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar strength combined with a weak risk-sensitive commodity currency is a global risk-off and tighter dollar-funding state. It hurts EM sovereign issuers and risk appetite generally.

COM.rationale: Energy issuers are a large share of the HY index and many EM sovereigns are oil exporters. Rising oil prices improve their credit quality.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions restrict credit supply and dealer balance sheets. This depresses subsequent risky-bond returns or reflects elevated risk premia.

ENDG.rationale: High-yield and EM bond indices show time-series momentum from slow price adjustment and illiquidity.

IR.rationale: Sharp rises in intermediate yields (taper-type rate shocks) trigger fund outflows and repricing in duration-sensitive EM and HY bonds, raising subsequent volatility.

B.rationale: Widening spreads with falling HY prices mark a credit sell-off. Such sell-offs cluster and amplify through redemptions and illiquidity.

V.rationale: Implied volatility is forward-looking, so it predicts realised volatility beyond past realised variance. Oil-volatility matters specifically for energy-heavy HY and oil-exporting EM sovereigns.

AP.rationale: Through the leverage effect, equity declines raise the volatility of firm and sovereign asset values and hence of credit returns.

ST.rationale: No clear mechanism links equity style factors to credit-index volatility.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation signals carry-trade unwinding and deleveraging, which is followed by turbulent risky-asset markets.

COM.rationale: Oil price slumps raise default risk and price dispersion in energy HY and petro-sovereign debt, increasing index volatility.

MC.rationale: Composite financial stress indices capture funding and liquidity strain, which predicts elevated volatility across credit markets.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clusters, and high recent realised variance tends to persist beyond simple linear decay.

IR.rationale: Abrupt rises in intermediate yields cause duration losses and outflows in EM sovereign and HY funds, raising the chance of a large drawdown.

B.rationale: An ongoing credit sell-off tends to continue through forced selling and illiquidity, fattening the left tail.

V.rationale: High equity and oil implied volatility signal a stressed, high-dispersion state in which large losses are more likely.

AP.rationale: Equity weakness in both US and EM leads credit deterioration because stocks price default risk faster.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry no clear information about credit-index tail losses.

FX.rationale: A strong broad dollar combined with yen appreciation is a classic risk-off, carry-unwind state. It tightens dollar funding for EM borrowers.

COM.rationale: Falling oil prices threaten energy issuers and oil-exporting sovereigns, raising the probability of large index losses.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress signals strained funding liquidity, under which credit markets are prone to large losses.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent returns persist in illiquid credit markets, so poor recent performance raises the chance of a further large loss.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to policy rates produce duration gains and an easing in funding conditions, supporting large positive returns.

B.rationale: Spread tightening with strong HY returns marks a credit rally. Such rallies persist, especially as spreads recover from wide levels.

V.rationale: Large gains occur mostly in high-volatility, high-risk-premium states, when relief rallies from depressed prices are possible.

AP.rationale: Strong US and EM equity returns lead credit rallies as improving default expectations are priced first in stocks.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry no clear information about credit-index upside tails.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar with a strong commodity currency signals easing global funding conditions and risk-on flows into EM and high-yield debt.

COM.rationale: Oil rebounds sharply improve the credit outlook of energy issuers and petro-sovereigns, which can drive large index gains.

MC.rationale: Large gains cluster after stress episodes, when spreads are wide and the compensation for risk is high.

ENDG.rationale: In stressed states, sharp declines are often followed by large rebounds as liquidity returns, so recent weakness widens the right tail as well.
